header.name: Britannia Industries Ltd
header.source: NSE closing price (end of day, not live); 52-week range computed from daily highs and lows (NSE bhavcopy)

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Britannia Industries (NSE: BRITANNIA) sells food products; its consolidated revenue in FY26 was ₹19,152 crore.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: In the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹5,598 crore, 15.6% more than a year earlier; the operating margin was 16.8% against 18.0%, and profit attributable to shareholders was ₹721 crore, 10.2% higher.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: On 6 Nov 2026, the first session after the result, BRITANNIA shares fell 3.92% while the NIFTY 50 rose 2.01% and the NIFTY FMCG index rose 0.67%; allowing for the market's move, BRITANNIA's own move was -5.21%, about 4.66 times its usual daily variation.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: These numbers measure the move, not its cause: the result, the FMCG sector's rise and any other news that day overlap, and nothing here separates them.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: At ₹4,754 (NSE close, 16 Nov 2026), a discounted cash flow model with a 8.98% cost of capital matches the price if revenue grows about 16.0% a year for five years at the FY26 operating margin of 16.7%; BRITANNIA's revenue grew 7.9% a year over FY22–FY26.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: That four-year rate is lifted by FY23's 15.3%; the three years since grew 2.9%, 7.0% and 6.7%.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: With the other assumptions at base, the valuation is most sensitive to the cost of capital (one percentage point either way: a model value of ₹2,421 to ₹4,053 a share) and to how long BRITANNIA keeps earning high returns on new investment (anywhere from returns equal to its cost of capital to a quarter above its past level: a model value of ₹1,909 to ₹3,063 a share); the Q3 FY27 result will be the next reported quarter.

prices.note: Each series is rebased to 100 on the first common session. Raw exchange prices are not published here (NSE terms).

metrics.label: Market cap
metrics.definition: Price × shares outstanding (share capital ÷ ₹1 face value at 2026-09-30).

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.definition: Price ÷ earnings per share over the last four reported quarters (Q3 FY26 – Q2 FY27).

metrics.label: EV / EBIT (TTM)
metrics.definition: Enterprise value (market cap − the net cash and treasury figure below) ÷ operating profit over the last four quarters.

metrics.label: Net cash and treasury
metrics.definition: Cash, bank balances and treasury investments, plus investments in joint ventures and associates, less lease liabilities, borrowings, preference shares and minority interests, at 30 Sep 2026.

metrics.label: Operating margin (FY26)
metrics.definition: EBIT ÷ revenue, after depreciation, excluding other income. Sites that quote an EBITDA-based margin show a higher figure.

metrics.label: ROE (FY26)
metrics.definition: Profit for the year ÷ total equity at year end.

metrics.label: ROIC (FY26)
metrics.definition: After-tax EBIT ÷ invested capital at the start of the year. Invested capital excludes about ₹3k crore of cash and treasury, which is why it looks so high.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY22–FY26
metrics.definition: Compound annual growth of revenue from FY22 to FY26. FY23 alone grew 15.3%; the three years since grew less.

metrics.label: Cash conversion (FY26)
metrics.definition: Operating cash flow ÷ profit for the year.

metrics.label: Beta vs NIFTY 50
metrics.definition: Sensitivity of BRITANNIA's daily return to the NIFTY 50's, over the two years to the price date.

scenarios.what: Revenue grows only at FY26's pace for five years, the operating margin slips 2 points, and growth after year 10 earns no more than its cost of capital.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.what: Revenue keeps its FY22-FY26 growth rate for five years, the FY26 margin holds, and BRITANNIA keeps its historical return on capital indefinitely.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.what: Revenue grows at H1 FY27's year-on-year pace for five years and the margin rises 1 point.

flags.title: The exchange's files contain errors
flags.text: 1 reconciliation checks fail on the exchange's own files, each with a recorded reason. They are marked as explained, not passed, and the figure as filed is used, never a corrected one.

flags.title: A cash-flow sign looks wrong in the FY22 file
flags.text: The exchange file for FY22 reports operating cash flow that differs from its parts by exactly the interest it files as paid inside operating activities, which looks like a sign error in the filing. The filed total is used and the check is shown as explained, not as passed.

limitations: Template A (non-financial, positive free cash flow). Single-stage fade model; no currency driver.
Cash flows are discounted to the balance-sheet date, 30 Sep 2026, two months before the price date; the model does not roll that gap forward, so its values are slightly low against the price.
The base growth anchor includes FY23's unusually large jump; later years grew more slowly.
Debt is borrowings plus lease liabilities; earmarked bank balances are counted as cash, which overstates cash slightly.
The risk-free rate is a twelve-month average while the price and equity risk premium are point-in-time.
The event study measures the size of a move, not its cause; five results days are too few for statistical claims.

Britannia's exchange XBRL filings carry no lease liabilities, so the lease liabilities in every year, the balance sheet of the latest half-year and the FY22 balance sheet come from the results PDFs (text layers checked against the printed subtotals and the XBRL).

Britannia's XBRL for FY22 is internally inconsistent: its operating cash flow differs from its components by exactly the interest it files as paid inside operating activities, which looks like a sign error in the filing. The filed operating cash flow total is used, and the check is shown as explained, not as passed.
Static page: prices are end-of-day as of the date shown, not live.
